acceptance: The last ledger advance and the list of missed merges are recorded in context
After the change, a mirror merge produces a successful reconciler run that advances ledger_head_sha (run id recorded)
Missed merges are replayed and a second replay leaves the ledger unchanged (test or recorded run)
A unit test covers the accepted commit shape and the refusal of a non-ancestor base
description:
## Problem
scripts/publication/reconciler.py verify_merge_commit rejects any commit with fewer than two parents ("expected 2+"), and corpus-event-bridge.yml refuses the same. The repository disallows merge commits (allow_merge_commit=false), so every published-results merge is a single-parent squash (mirror #4114 landed as 4331a43a54 with one parent). corpus-event-bridge.yml has zero runs in its history, and the hourly corpus-reconciler schedule runs with no events file and exits "no events" (last 30 runs 'success', none processed anything). The ledger (publication/ledger.json, ledger_head_sha) and publication generation have therefore not advanced for any recent merge, manual or automated. The results mirror workflow now merges validated mirrors automatically, which makes this gap matter more.

## Decision gate
- Agent: confirm from published-results history when the ledger last advanced and which merges it missed.
- Then choose one (owner confirms, because it changes the publication ledger contract):
  1. Teach the reconciler and bridge to accept a squash commit, taking the first parent as the base, and have the mirror workflow dispatch the reconciler after its merge (GITHUB_TOKEN pushes do not trigger the bridge).
  2. Allow merge commits for published-results only (ruleset or merge-method restriction), keeping develop squash-only.
- Replay the missed merges into the ledger in order.

## Guardrails
- The reconciler must still refuse a commit whose base is not an ancestor, and must not accept a commit that is not on published-results.
- No rewrite of published-results history.
- Ledger replay is idempotent: running it twice produces the same ledger.
